data.body:
Plan-review RCA (orchestrator, after 7 BLOCK rounds) — the plan premise was WRONG about a load-bearing dependency.

The plan said: remove Mode.RECONCILE_CHECK from the enum plus its _ORDERED and MODE_CAPS entries, while preserving the _ref_lock pause sentinel gated_mode=="reconcile-check" byte-for-byte. Those two are CONTRADICTORY.

Evidence (src):
- _advisory_lock._mode_blocks() (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_advisory_lock.py:257) reads the pause-gate blob and computes blocking via `gated_mode = mode_mod.Mode.from_str(gated_mode_str)` then `target_mode > gated_mode`. gated_mode_str is the literal "reconcile-check".
- mode.py:_ORDERED (line 21) lists "reconcile-check" first; Mode ordering uses _ORDERED.index(value). from_str requires the enum member.
- So a paused repo (gate blob gated_mode=="reconcile-check", written at _ref_lock.py:717) is read BACK through Mode.from_str("reconcile-check"). Remove the enum/_ORDERED entry and from_str raises ValueError -> _mode_blocks logs "unrecognised mode; treating as no gate" -> returns False -> THE PAUSE STOPS BLOCKING. Live behavioral regression.

Decision (correctness-driven scope refinement): RETAIN Mode.RECONCILE_CHECK (enum member + _ORDERED entry + MODE_CAPS entry + from_str support) as a load-bearing INTERNAL gate/pause mode. It is NOT unused, so retaining it is consistent with the "remove deprecated/UNUSED surface" goal. REMOVE only:
- the legacy `rebar reconcile --mode reconcile-check` CLI command surface (_cli parser/registry/help),
- the `--filter-local-ids` CLI surface,
- `_run_reconcile_check` direct-engine dispatch branch + its .bridge_state/reconcile-check.json writer (__main__.py),
- the orphaned `reconcile_check.py` discrepancy-report module (and its dedicated tests),
- the `reconcile_diagnostics` status/model/schema field (last_pass.py reader, _mcp_models.py, bridge_status.schema.json, types.py),
- repoint _bridge_runner MODE_COMMANDS["reconcile-check"] to `rebar bridge preview`.

Consequence: this SHRINKS test churn. All `Mode.RECONCILE_CHECK` references (test_mode.py, test_reconcile_once.py, test_recovery_write_boundary.py, test_advisory_lock.py, test_orchestrator_wiring.py, ...) STAY VALID because the enum is retained — plan-review finding 3 (migrate advisory_lock tests off the enum) is thereby moot. Only the reconcile_check-module tests (test_reconcile_check*.py) and the filter-CLI test (test_reconcile_filter.py) need deletion/migration.

Plan + file_impact rewritten accordingly.
